knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Dimension-order mapping mismatch during graph export of parameterized operations
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Export and graph transformation APIs may misinterpret dimension-indexed parameters when source framework and target runtime use different axis ordering conventions, especially for operations whose parameters are specified from the last dimension backwards.

risk_dimensions.shape: Higher-rank tensors where dimension-indexed parameters target non-last axes; dynamic axes that prevent static validation of dimension mapping
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Dynamic dimension export paths that bypass static shape checks

failure_mechanism.description: The exporter translates dimension-indexed operation parameters into target graph operations using an incorrect axis mapping convention, causing the transformed graph to apply the operation along unintended axes.

input_exploration: Vary tensor ranks, especially higher-rank tensors with more than two dimensions
Vary which dimensions receive non-default operation parameters
Combine parameterized dimension operations with dynamic axes
Use shapes that make dimension-order mistakes observable in output values
constraint_awareness: Dimension-indexed parameters may follow last-dimension-first ordering
Target runtimes may expect axes in a different order than the source framework
Parameter tuple length usually depends on tensor rank and must remain consistent
Dynamic axes can hide axis mapping errors during export-time validation
oracle_strategy: Execute the original framework model to obtain a reference output
Run the exported graph in the target runtime and compare outputs numerically
Treat any mismatch as an incorrect graph transformation or export defect

transferability.reason: Many export and graph transformation paths translate dimension-specific parameters such as padding, slicing, concatenation, and normalization axes. The same axis ordering mismatch can affect any API that lowers a framework operation with dimension-indexed arguments to a backend or runtime with different axis conventions.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Generate harnesses that systematically vary tensor ranks and the axis targeted by dimension-indexed parameters. Include dynamic axes and compare source framework outputs against exported runtime outputs. Focus on operations where parameter order is defined relative to the last dimension.
generation_strategy: Create parameterized modules wrapping dimension-sensitive operations, export them through graph transformation APIs, and use differential testing between the source framework and target runtime. Generalize dimension-indexed parameters rather than hardcoding specific padding tuples.
